blogs.title: When “Angioedema” Isn’t: Recognizing Pseudoangioedema in Dermatomyositis
blogs.description: Neck and facial swelling that doesn’t fit histamine- or bradykinin-mediated angioedema should trigger a myositis search. This post lays out bedside red flags (subacute course, non-tender edema, dysphagia, abnormal nailfolds/rash, proximal weakness), labs to send immediately (CK, transaminases, LDH), and a pragmatic ED-to-ward algorithm to pivot from ENT/infectious workups to inflammatory myopathy, preventing airway delays and diagnostic drift.

blogs.title: Decoding Anti-SAE1 Dermatomyositis: Phenotype, Pitfalls, and Prognosis
blogs.description: A deep dive into the anti-SAE1 autoantibody: expected cutaneous patterns, high rates of dysphagia and ILD, and the nuanced (but real) malignancy signal. We’ll discuss assay variability (e.g., line blot interpretation), how SAE1 phenotypes differ from MDA5 and TIF1-γ disease, and how to translate a positive result into concrete monitoring plans for muscle, lung, skin, and cancer risk.

blogs.title: Swallow First, Ask Questions Later: Airway and Dysphagia Management in Inflammatory Myopathy
blogs.description: Dysphagia can be the most dangerous organ involvement in dermatomyositis. Using this case, we review recognizing extrathoracic restrictive patterns on PFTs, interpreting videofluoroscopy, preventing aspiration pneumonitis, and coordinating ENT, speech pathology, and immunosuppression. Practical tips include when to escalate to pulse steroids/IVIG, nutrition strategies (NG vs PEG), secretion control, and how to time therapy while protecting the airway.

blogs.title: Lighting Up the Muscles: How MRI and FDG-PET Guide Myositis Diagnosis (and Exclude Mimics)
blogs.description: Imaging clarified this case: MRI localized active myositis; FDG-PET showed diffuse myositis and helped exclude occult malignancy. We compare MRI vs PET for sensitivity, anatomical mapping, and treatment response tracking, and review muscle biopsy hallmarks (perifascicular necrosis and capillary C5b-9) that seal the dermatomyositis diagnosis. We also address interpreting pulmonary nodules and peribronchial consolidation as aspiration sequelae, not primary ILD or cancer.

blogs.title: Designing the Immunosuppression Playbook: Steroids, IVIG, Mycophenolate, Rituximab—and PJP Prophylaxis
blogs.description: Stepwise management when myositis threatens the airway: pulse methylpred, early IVIG, and selecting a steroid-sparing agent. We discuss why methotrexate may be avoided with abnormal lung tests, evidence and pragmatics for mycophenolate vs azathioprine vs tacrolimus vs rituximab, CK and strength-based tapering, and real-world PJP prophylaxis options when TMP-SMX causes trouble (e.g., inhaled pentamidine) with monitoring tips.

blogs.title: Dermatomyositis and Cancer: Applying IMACS Risk-Stratified Screening at the Bedside
blogs.description: Translating guidelines into action: using dermatomyositis subtype, dysphagia, sex, and autoantibodies (including SAE1) to assign malignancy risk and build a screening bundle. We outline a practical pathway—baseline CT chest/abdomen/pelvis or PET-CT, age-appropriate screening, targeted endoscopy, tumor markers’ limits—and propose follow-up intervals and triggers to re-image. A case-based template you can drop into your discharge and clinic plans.
